title: Design the experience before the interface
statement: Design what students will see, hear, examine and think about before the interface, and make the interface serve that experience rather than varying layouts without it.
example: All five layout drafts, each of which had passed its interaction checks, were rejected in review.
detail: Five alternative layouts for the Grade 9 unit's app passed their interaction checks, with visual browser checks still unverified (`g9/transcript/chat-transcript.redacted.txt`, lines 4944-4946), and when asked to pick one, review rejected all five (lines 5368 and 5397). Later builds drew the same complaint (line 6733). The direction was then reset to the experience described, a mature illustrated-book experience with rich scenes worth examining, compelling narration, quiet optional help and space for students to think, with the interface serving it (line 6754), and the reset was endorsed (line 6775).
against: The reset direction was not finished or tried with students, and the rejections are a single review's judgment.

evidence.quote: Interaction checks passed; visual browser QA remains unverified.
I’ve been producing interface variations instead of the experience you described.
